plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as gradual variation in peak sharpness and late-time curvature among trajectories with comparable early rise; in holdout, stronger or longer irradiation histories extend this into delayed versus early saturation of daughter loss that the fixed-capacity parent cannot match with one shared parameter set.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the capacity-evolution effect is turned off so the capacity remains constant over the experiment, or in the limit where its evolution is much slower than the observation window.
plan.promotion_reason: A fixed damage_capacity enforces one shared saturation scale for the daughter-loss environment. To represent irradiation-history-dependent carrying capacity of that environment, the capacity itself must evolve as a state; existing states cannot encode this without changing the target mapping only trivially.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the saturation scale of the daughter-loss environment is fixed, but in irradiated media the available loss pathways or trapping/escape structure can themselves grow or anneal during the run.
plan.baseline_assumption: The finite saturation scale damage_capacity is time independent and unaffected by irradiation history.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Radiation-induced restructuring changes the number of effective daughter-removal sites or channels, so the environment controlling daughter loss has an evolving capacity rather than a fixed one.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-capacity assumption rather than adding an unrelated source or sink. The current target mapping already includes history dependence through daughter_decay_constant, but all trajectories are forced toward the same maximum effective loss scale set by one constant damage_capacity. Varying the irradiation history through the observed N_D trajectory while holding parent_decay_constant, initial N_P, and initial daughter_decay_constant fixed can therefore only change how quickly that fixed ceiling is approached, not the ceiling itself. If damage_capacity is promoted to a state, then accumulated daughter presence can alter the eventual saturation scale of daughter loss. This changes the scored mapping consequentially: dN_D_dt at later times no longer depends only on N_P, N_D, and the current daughter_decay_constant under one fixed ceiling, but on whether the environment has expanded or relaxed its capacity during the trajectory. The observable contrast is a changed daughter peak and post-peak curvature reachable under the stated initial conditions when daughter-driven environmental evolution is moderate. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both delayed saturation with prolonged daughter residence and earlier stronger depletion across such conditions, because it has only one fixed saturation scale for all runs. Limitation: if capacity evolution is extremely slow or negligible on the observation window, the refinement collapses back to the parent and may not be distinguishable.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when the daughter population becomes comparable to or larger than the instantaneous removal-environment scale, i.e. N_D/damage_capacity is not small over part of the sampled window; if N_D stays well below damage_capacity throughout, the parent linear law remains an adequate approximation.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate daughter loads can already show slight peak broadening relative to a linear sink; in holdout, runs reaching higher N_D/damage_capacity amplify the same occupancy-limited curvature rather than introducing a new mechanism.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the low-occupancy limit N_D/damage_capacity << 1, where the refined sink reduces to approximately daughter_decay_constant*N_D.
plan.gap_statement: The current model lets daughter removal remain exactly first-order in daughter abundance even when the same evolving environment is already modeled as having a finite capacity, omitting occupancy-limited processing of daughters by that environment.
plan.baseline_assumption: The daughter-removal flux is proportional to N_D at all daughter loads, with no saturation or crowding in the realized removal rate once daughter_decay_constant and damage_capacity are specified.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite trapping, recombination, escape, or removal channels can become occupied or throughput-limited, so the realized daughter loss per unit time increases sublinearly with daughter abundance when many daughters compete for the same finite environment.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the idealized first-order daughter-loss assumption rather than adding a wholly new process. The parent already acknowledges an evolving finite damage capacity, but its scored target mapping still uses a linear sink daughter_decay_constant*N_D, which implies unlimited proportional throughput at any daughter burden. Vary the regime through trajectories that differ in attained N_D/damage_capacity while holding the same governing parameter set and initial-condition contract otherwise fixed. Under the current law, once N_P and daughter_decay_constant are matched, the local dependence of dN_D_dt on N_D is always a single negative slope. Under the refined occupancy-limited law, the sink term bends: at low load it matches the parent, while at higher load the incremental sink gained from additional daughters weakens. This changes the target mapping itself, not just auxiliary states, because the N_D dependence of dN_D_dt is altered directly. The effect is scientifically admissible when daughter burden reaches a non-small fraction of the available removal scale; if not, this refinement is effectively latent and the parent remains a valid approximation.

plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit of negligible self-shielding, i.e. when the added attenuation strength tends to zero or throughout regimes with N_D small enough that all daughters are effectively equally exposed.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes every daughter nucleus experiences the same removal accessibility once crowding is summarized by a single throughput-limited environment, omitting additional shielding or inaccessibility that can arise when daughter accumulation itself obstructs exposure to removal channels.
plan.baseline_assumption: The daughter-loss environment is fully characterized by the existing occupancy-limited factor 1 + N_D/damage_capacity, with no extra daughter-induced reduction in accessibility beyond that throughput saturation.
plan.scientific_mechanism: At high daughter loading, accumulated daughters can partially shield, trap, or bury one another so that a growing fraction resides in less accessible microenvironments; removal then falls off more strongly with N_D than the current single occupancy factor allows.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to change the daughter-removal assumption rather than add an unrelated source or sink. Vary time so that the observed trajectory spans low to high daughter abundance under the same initial conditions and fixed parent_decay_constant, damage-drive, and capacity parameters. In the parent, once N_P is fixed at any instant, the daughter contribution to dN_D_dt is controlled by one occupancy scale N_D/damage_capacity and therefore has a single saturating curvature. In the refined model, the same supplied states can produce weaker effective removal at larger N_D because daughters become less accessible to the loss channels, not merely because channels are throughput-limited. The observable contrast is a broader buildup region and delayed onset of strong depletion when N_D reaches the capacity scale. This is scientifically admissible in dense irradiated or trapping environments, but the effect may be unresolvable if trajectories stay in N_D << damage_capacity. No new state is needed because the omitted mechanism can be represented as a different instantaneous dependence of the target mapping on existing states rather than requiring an independently evolving memory variable.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories the mechanism appears late in runs after daughter buildup, where equal N_D can correspond to different daughter_decay_constant histories; in holdout it extends to stronger damage-drive or weaker relaxation conditions that push environment_load higher and accentuate the curvature change.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit daughter_decay_constant/damage_capacity -> 0, where environmental overdamage never throttles the realized daughter-loss term.
plan.gap_statement: The current model lets the effective daughter removal rate keep acting linearly in the target once daughter_decay_constant has been built up, aside from occupancy and self-shielding by N_D itself; it omits saturation of the removal environment's own throughput when the accumulated damage state becomes large relative to available capacity.
plan.baseline_assumption: The realized daughter-loss flux is fully determined by daughter occupancy/self-shielding and scales linearly with the history-dependent effective daughter_decay_constant, regardless of how saturated that damage state is relative to damage_capacity.
plan.scientific_mechanism: As radiation damage accumulates, removal sites/channels can become structurally degraded, congested, or mutually interfering, so a high effective daughter-loss environment does not translate into proportionally high daughter removal once the environment is itself near capacity.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's assumption that the damage-built removal environment remains perfectly effective once created. Hold fixed the parent source law parent_decay_constant*N_P and compare times or parameter settings that produce similar observed N_P and N_D but different accumulated environment_load = daughter_decay_constant/damage_capacity. The current target mapping uses only one suppression coordinate based on daughter_loading = N_D/damage_capacity, so after refitting one shared parameter set it cannot create a distinct additional downturn tied specifically to high environment_load at the same daughter loading. The refined child mapping would change the target itself, not merely auxiliary trajectories, by making daughter loss bend over when the removal environment is overdriven. This is scientifically admissible in regimes with substantial damage buildup and finite restructuring capacity; it is not expected to matter when damage remains small, which also provides a clear parent-recovery limit.

response_change.parent_relation: The daughter loss term depends only on the instantaneous daughter loading N_D relative to a single evolving capacity, so for a given observed pair (N_P,N_D) the target slope changes smoothly with one occupancy-controlled suppression profile.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same parent-production term but refine the daughter-loss environment so that damage-driven removal efficiency is additionally throttled when the removal environment itself becomes highly damaged relative to its capacity, making the target depend on the joint state (N_D, daughter_decay_constant, damage_capacity) through a second internal saturation.
response_change.observable_effect: At comparable N_P and N_D, runs reaching high daughter_decay_constant/damage_capacity show an earlier flattening and softer post-peak depletion of N_D than the parent law predicts, because removal self-saturates through environmental overdamage rather than only through daughter occupancy.

diagnostic_groups.name: daughter_loading
diagnostic_groups.role: Current occupancy/self-shielding control already used by the parent target mapping

diagnostic_groups.name: environment_load
diagnostic_groups.role: Degree to which the effective daughter-loss environment is itself driven near saturation and can no longer convert additional damage into proportionally higher removal

contract.activation_condition: Observable when irradiation history drives daughter_decay_constant/damage_capacity to order one while N_D/damage_capacity is also non-negligible; weak or absent in the low-damage regime daughter_decay_constant << damage_capacity.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training trajectories the mechanism appears late in runs after daughter buildup, where equal N_D can correspond to different daughter_decay_constant histories; in holdout it extends to stronger damage-drive or weaker relaxation conditions that push environment_load higher and accentuate the curvature change.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit daughter_decay_constant/damage_capacity -> 0, where environmental overdamage never throttles the realized daughter-loss term.
contract.domain_mechanism: finite-capacity saturation of the damage-built daughter-removal environment
contract.scientific_mechanism: As radiation damage accumulates, removal sites/channels can become structurally degraded, congested, or mutually interfering, so a high effective daughter-loss environment does not translate into proportionally high daughter removal once the environment is itself near capacity.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a second state-dependent saturation coordinate in the scored target law. A single retuned occupancy profile cannot reproduce both low-environment-load and high-environment-load curvature at the same observed N_P and N_D with one shared parameter set.
contract.assumption_before: The realized daughter-loss flux remains linear in daughter_decay_constant once that internal damage state is established, with only daughter-occupancy suppression modulating it.
contract.assumption_after: The realized daughter-loss flux is additionally throttled when daughter_decay_constant itself approaches damage_capacity, representing finite throughput of an overdriven removal environment.
contract.parent_reduction: In the limit daughter_decay_constant/damage_capacity -> 0, the extra denominator factor approaches 1 and the parent expression is recovered.
contract.observable_signature: Holding the parent source term relation fixed, compare portions of trajectories with similar N_P and N_D but different environment_load = daughter_decay_constant/damage_capacity. The successor predicts smaller-magnitude daughter loss, hence earlier flattening and softer post-peak decline, specifically in the high-environment-load case; the parent predicts the same loss whenever N_P, N_D, and damage_capacity imply the same occupancy suppression regardless of environment_load.
contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all existing parent parameters cannot create a separate target dependence on environment_load at fixed daughter_loading, because the parent scored mapping contains only one suppression coordinate N_D/damage_capacity multiplying a linear daughter_decay_constant factor. One shared parent parameter set therefore cannot simultaneously match low- and high-environment-load segments that share similar N_P and N_D but differ in realized loss throttling.
